skill.description: Create distributable Python packages with modern project structure, pyproject.toml metadata, build artifacts, and PyPI publishing guidance.
skill.summary: Guide Python package layout, build configuration, CLI entry points, distribution files, and publishing workflows.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and visible documentation URLs. The confirmed risk is credential handling guidance around ~/.pypirc, which can persist PyPI tokens outside the project. No prompt injection or covert exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: PyPI token examples are stored in ~/.pypirc.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Trusted Publishing or scoped tokens stored in CI secrets or a password manager. If ~/.pypirc is used, require restrictive permissions and never commit it.

remediation.issue: Publishing and install commands can change external package indexes or upload artifacts.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit user confirmation before running pip install, twine upload, or private-index commands.

remediation.issue: Private index examples can hide dependency confusion risks.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to verify index ownership, package names, and fallback behavior before using extra-index-url.

content.value_statement: Python packaging requires correct metadata, build tools, and release steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through package layout, builds, and publishing.
actual_capabilities: Plans source-layout, flat-layout, namespace, and multi-package project structures.
Drafts pyproject.toml metadata, dependencies, optional extras, scripts, and classifiers.
Shows build backend patterns for setuptools, setuptools-scm, hatchling-style metadata, and C extensions.
Guides local builds, wheel and source distribution checks, editable installs, and isolated install tests.
Provides PyPI, TestPyPI, private index, GitHub Actions, README, MANIFEST.in, and .gitignore examples.
limitations: It provides guidance and templates; it does not verify package ownership or PyPI permissions.
Publishing and install commands can affect remote repositories and local environments.
Token examples must be replaced with secure, project-specific credential handling.
Generated metadata still needs legal, license, and maintainer review before release.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Library Release
use_cases.description: Create package metadata, build artifacts, and release checks for a Python library.

use_cases.title: Create a Python CLI Package
use_cases.description: Define entry points, CLI module structure, dependencies, and install tests for a command-line tool.

use_cases.title: Standardize Internal Packages
use_cases.description: Set up private index publishing, consistent project layout, CI builds, and dependency conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic Python package structure for my project. Include pyproject.toml, src layout, tests, README, and build steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add CLI Packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this Python module into an installable CLI package. Add entry points, dependencies, usage notes, and installation tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for PyPI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this package for PyPI release readiness. Check metadata, classifiers, dependencies, build outputs, docs, and TestPyPI workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Design packaging for a multi-package Python project with namespace packages, optional extras, generated versions, CI wheels, and private index publishing.

output_examples.input: I need to publish a small Python library.
output_examples.output: A release plan with src layout, pyproject.toml fields, dependency groups, build commands, validation steps, and PyPI publishing checkpoints.

output_examples.input: My script should install as a terminal command.
output_examples.output: A CLI packaging plan with module layout, entry point naming, argument parser placement, test strategy, and install verification steps.

output_examples.input: Our team uses a private package index.
output_examples.output: Guidance for private index configuration, secure credential handling, dependency confusion warnings, and CI upload controls.

best_practices: Use src layout and pyproject.toml for new distributable packages.
Build and test packages in a clean virtual environment before publishing.
Use scoped tokens or trusted publishing, and keep release credentials out of source control.
anti_patterns: Publishing directly to production PyPI before testing installation from TestPyPI.
Hardcoding real tokens, private index credentials, or maintainer secrets in project files.
Using exact dependency pins for libraries unless reproducibility requires them.

faq.question: Does this skill publish packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and checks, but publishing should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does it support pyproject.toml?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on modern pyproject.toml metadata and build-system configuration.

faq.question: Can it help with CLI tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Click, argparse, project scripts, entry points, and install testing.

faq.question: Can it handle private package indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes private index examples, but credentials and index trust must be reviewed.

faq.question: Does it replace package security review?
faq.answer: No. It does not audit dependencies, ownership, malware risk, or release permissions.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
